items.summary: his work studies the basin geometry of the negative integer Collatz map. Under exact iteration of T(n)={n/2,n even,3n+1,n odd,T(n)= \begin{cases} n/2, & n \text{ even},\\ 3n+1, & n \text{ odd}, \end{cases} the first 10710^7 negative integers are observed to enter one of the three classical negative cycles through −1-1 , −5-5 , and −17-17 . The corresponding empirical basin proportions stabilize near 0.327:0.324:0.3480.327:0.324:0.348 , with a persistent modest excess for the C−17C_{-17} basin. The paper then examines the structure behind these basin frequencies. Basin membership is found to be weakly predicted by simple residue classes modulo 2k2^k , and short prefixes of the 22 -adic valuation itinerary under the accelerated odd Collatz map show essentially no transferable predictive power in held-out tests. A markedly different structure appears in the reverse dynamics. Monotone inverse trees rooted in the three negative attractors show strongly unequal relative sizes, stabilizing near 0.293:0.218:0.4890.293:0.218:0.489 . The associated tree-count ratios remain highly stable over repeated increases in the magnitude cutoff, motivating a common reverse-growth conjecture with basin-dependent amplitudes. Forward trajectories partially erase this reverse-tree asymmetry. Low-reversal trajectories are strongly enriched for the C−17C_{-17} attractor, while increasing non-monotone trajectory complexity attenuates that advantage and moves the observed basin shares closer to the near-balanced global census. The resulting empirical picture is that asymmetric reverse accessibility and forward trajectory mixing jointly shape the macroscopic basin distribution. The paper proposes corresponding conjectures on negative basin densities and reverse-tree ratio convergence. These computations do not prove that every negative integer enters one of the three known cycles, do not exclude additional negative cycles or divergent orbits, and do not resolve the positive Collatz conjecture. The contribution is a computational study of basin structure, reverse accessibility, and mixing in the signed integer extension of the Collatz map.
items.title: Negative-Basin Geometry in the Integer Collatz Map: Forward Census, Reverse-Tree Asymmetry, and Mixing

items.summary: The coordination of Automated Guided Vehicles (AGVs) in high-density industrial environments represents a critical challenge within Logistics 4.0, as traditional traffic management methods often lead to inefficiencies caused by negotiation-based priority assignment. To overcome the resulting limitations, this paper presents an innovative AGV traffic management system based on a Lifelong Multi-Agent Path Finding (L-MAPF) algorithm operating on roadmaps generated with Non-Uniform Rational B-Splines (NURBS) curves. The approach guarantees locally optimal coordination and ensures safe operation of large and heterogeneous AGVs. Building on this concept, the proposed framework integrates a modified version of the Bounded Horizon Conflict Based Search (CBS) technique within a Rolling Horizon Conflict Resolution strategy, utilizing an extended time horizon for each agent to enable effective conflict resolution in corridors identified by a topological map. In contrast to state-of-the-art methods for AGV fleet traffic management, the proposed solution is designed for real-world, non-standardized (i.e., non-grid-like) industrial settings characterized by narrow bidirectional corridors and high-traffic density, where AGVs of various sizes and capabilities operate simultaneously. Key contributions include an anytime conflict resolution strategy with adaptive time horizon regulation, an execution layer for safe and standard-compliant interaction with real AGVs, and an advanced mechanism for deadlock detection and resolution. Experimental results obtained in realistic industrial environments demonstrate higher throughput, with improvements of up to 11% over a conventional rule-based traffic management system, a state-of-the-art industrial method, and a priority-based L-MAPF variant, while maintaining continuous operation and improved efficiency.
items.title: A traffic management system for large and heterogeneous vehicles in narrow industrial environments

items.summary: We study explicit algebraic cycles and the recovery of their supports in three special fourfold settings. For a smooth diagonal intersection of five quadrics in P⁹, a paired splitting plane in the associated ten-hyperplane arrangement produces an orbit of thirty-two degree-four del Pezzo surfaces. Their alternating rational cycle w has square 3. An elliptic-quartic net gives an actual correspondence D = w × η to P² and the Chow projector w × w/3. The paired incidence is smooth of dimension twelve, finite and locally immersed over the sixteen-dimensional diagonal moduli space, and has a nonempty non-evaluation open. Its tangent quotient is an Artinian reduction of the Segre ring of P² × P², with Hilbert function (1, 4, 1). We use this quotient and the relative cycles to identify the complete marked Hodge germ with the paired incidence branch, including its scheme structure. At a very general paired point, the full-character rational Hodge sector is exactly ℚw; the proper characters give the rational Hodge conjecture for these very general fourfolds. The germ statement concerns diagonal deformations. For hypersurface fourfolds of degree d ≥ 5, we prove a reverse recognition theorem. A tangent-exhausting integrated Hodge family with a persistent embedded connected-sum annihilator forces its two candidate ambient planes to lie on the hypersurface and recovers the full rationally weighted primitive class. The conormal variation is surjective onto the true graded ideal-deformation space and has a seventeen-dimensional kernel. An explicit smooth family shows that the equation can nevertheless fail to belong to the square of its Hodge annihilator. Finally, from Paranjape's K3–Prym correspondence we construct a quadratic trace and an explicit sheared odd correspondence, purify it by rational endomorphism selectors, and compute its full and primitive kernels under a stated full Hodge-group hypothesis. Weil-class algebraicity is already known; this part concerns an explicit realization and its action. Further constructions record exact Chow returns and several rigidity phenomena. All genericity restrictions and the distinction between Chow identities, complex Hodge dimensions, and rational Hodge spaces are retained.
items.title: Explicit Hodge Classes and Support Recognition on Special Fourfolds

items.summary: Generative AI makes it easier for one person to write like another. That familiar observation is only the entry point here. My concern is with what may happen before a sentence appears: the selection of distinctions, the ordering of values, and the judgment by which a person decides that this, rather than something else, is worth saying. I use Person-Anchored Constructivism in the Age of Subjectivity Homogenization for the theory developed in this article. It describes the lifelong formation and re-formation of a Personal Construct Order by a concrete person. Experience, judgment, choice, and responsibility are not four variables added to that order. They are what keep it anchored in the person whose order it is. Subjectivity Homogenization names the condition in which shared forms of expression or evaluation begin to take over that constructive work. I distinguish three places at which this may happen: expression, judgment, and the order governing a person's constructs. To make this distinction, I draw on personal construct psychology, research on writing as thinking, reflexivity, and participatory sense-making. I also separate the Personal Construct System from its ordering dimension, the Personal Construct Order. The process connecting these claims is the Subjectivity Reconstruction Loop: The Concrete Person → Personal Construct Order → Reflexive Construing → Construct Externalization → Intersubjective Loop → Emergence of Discrepancy → Construct Recalibration → Reconstruction of the Person. Repeated completion of that loop constitutes the Individuation of Subjectivity. Eight propositions set out how homogenization, person-anchoring, and reconstruction are related. This record contains the English preprint and a complete Chinese translation.

items.summary: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) has emerged as a pivotal paradigm for complex decision-making in autonomous systems and air combat. While MARL has demonstrated significant potential in air combat, achieving sophisticated tactical coordination remains a non-trivial challenge. This difficulty is largely attributed to two primary limitations: (1) the absence of structured relational modeling hinders agents from capturing complex, time-varying interactions among battlefield entities; and (2) conventional flat architectures often lack the capability to explicitly model tactical roles, leading to ambiguous task allocation in highly dynamic environments. To address these challenges, we propose Hierarchical Dynamic Role-Graph Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (DRG-MAPPO), a novel MARL framework that integrates graph-based relational modeling with dynamic role assignment. Specifically, DRG-MAPPO constructs a graph-based representation of battlefield interactions and leverages graph attention mechanisms to extract critical relational features among allies, enemies, and threats. Subsequently, a high-level policy employs a dynamic role assignment mechanism to determine tactical responsibilities (e.g., ``leader'' and ``supporter''). Conditioned on these roles and encoded graph-relational features, a low-level policy executes discrete maneuver actions, facilitating the joint optimization of tactical strategy and collaborative execution. Furthermore, a target-priority auxiliary task is designed to foster the emergence of behaviors such as focus-fire. Experimental results demonstrate that DRG-MAPPO achieves a state-of-the-art win rate of 87%, suggesting that our framework effectively balances relational modeling, interpretability, and optimization stability for cooperative air combat.
items.title: DRG-MAPPO: Hierarchical Dynamic Role-Graph Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Cooperative Air Combat

items.summary: Generative AI is reshaping how research software is developed. Tools and patterns ranging from “vibe coding” through the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and autonomous agents now offer compelling productivity gains, but their adoption in scientific computing surfaces failure modes that general-purpose evaluation does not catch: silent unit conversions, violated conservation laws, hallucinated physics, loss of numerical precision, and quietly broken reproducibility. These failures share a signature: nothing visible goes wrong. The AI ecosystem itself is moving fast, leaving RSEs to make consequential integration decisions with little shared vocabulary or principled guidance. This talk introduces Scientific Agentic Engineering , the central contribution of an in-progress 2026 Better Scientific Software (BSSw) Fellowship: a tool-agnostic methodology for integrating AI agents into high-stakes scientific software workflows. The framework defines how agents, scientific skills, and MCP servers should be structured around validation loops, explicit human-in-the-loop checkpoints, and domain-specific safeguards. Every task moves through a short workflow (frame, plan and critique, implement, verify), with decisions recorded throughout, and the framework maps each documented failure mode to the stage where it is cheapest to catch. The intent is not to recommend any particular AI tool but to articulate foundational concepts that remain valid as the underlying technology changes. I will share three artifacts from the fellowship: The Framework (published July 2026). Shared vocabulary, its principles and workflow, structural guidance on where safeguards live, and a pattern catalog of named practices, each tied to the failure it counters. The Reference Workflow. A structured exercise in which RSEs use AI tools to build a small weather-model error-statistics application, applying the framework to avoid the failure modes it documents. The Community Repository. A curated starter set of scientific MCP server templates, agent skills such as unit checkers and conservation-law validators, and agent configuration examples, designed to be starting points for the community to adapt to a variety of scientific domains. These artifacts are by design community resources, and broader adoption is the explicit aim of the remaining milestones, which include an interactive online tutorial series comparing purpose-built scientific agents with general-purpose tools, a recorded live workshop published for asynchronous access, and a BSSw.io blog post directing the community to the project’s resources. This work engages the conference theme directly by advancing AI-assisted scientific software development from ad-hoc experimentation toward a disciplined, transferable engineering practice.
items.title: Scientific Agentic Engineering: A Framework for Reliable AI Agents in Research Software

items.summary: This record contains the preprint paper "LOST IN THE PDFS: CONTEXT DEGRADATION AND PARAMETRIC HALLUCINATIONS IN LLM UIS" , authored by Gabriele D’Iorio (University of Naples Parthenope).  The study investigates the structural limitations and operational vulnerabilities of commercial web-based Large Language Model (LLM) interfaces when handling long, multi-document sequential workflows in educational contexts. Abstract: The growing use of LLMs for educational purposes, especially by inexperienced users, inevitably leads to LLMs hallucinating and making mistakes. This study presents an experiment using the web version of Gemini (Pro Standard and Flash Standard modes) to simulate a numerical analysis class covering three topics (interpolation, piecewise interpolation, and approximation), each in a separate PDF. This study is subdivided into two scenarios created to evaluate how the LLM responded and, above all, to see how long it took to hallucinate or suffer from context degradation. The results demonstrate the failure of both scenarios due to context degradation. Despite large theoretical context windows, sudden attachment truncation in the web UI forces the model to rely on its parametric memory, leading to severe hallucinations and sycophantic behavior. Key Topics Covered: - Context Degradation & "Lost in the Middle" Phenomenon: Analysis of how LLMs lose retrieval accuracy in prolonged sessions. - Parametric Hallucinations: How models compensate for context loss by fabricating details from pre-training data. - Document Parsing Challenges: Visual layout issues in standard Web UIs. - Experimental Evaluation: A comparative analysis of a single-chat setup (Scenario A) versus a dual-agent/tutor setup (Scenario B). Data Availability: The comprehensive dataset, interaction logs, prompt configurations, and Python scripts used for token counting are openly accessible in the project’s GitHub repository at: https://github.com/gabpolymath/lost_in_the_pdfs/
items.title: Lost in the PDFs: Context Degradation and Parametric Hallucinations in LLM UIs

items.summary: Collective intelligence depends not only on the capabilities of individual members, but also on how those members are organized. Yet artificial multi-agent systems are typically assembled using fixed organizational structures, even when the physical tasks they perform impose fundamentally different coordination requirements. Here we show that principles from human organization theory can be operationalized to organize large, heterogeneous collectives of embodied artificial agents. We introduce ORCH (Organizing Roles and Coordination Hierarchies), which constructs task-specific hierarchical organizations by combining pooled interdependence for work that can proceed concurrently with sequential interdependence for work governed by prerequisite relationships. Across 25 wildfire-response missions spanning reconnaissance, rescue, transportation, resource management, containment and suppression, we evaluated teams of up to 50 heterogeneous agents using eight large language models. Organizations constructed using these principles consistently outperformed four representative embodied multi-agent approaches across mission outcome, execution efficiency, exploration and computational resource use. Human-designed ORCH organizations improved final score by 63.97% and execution efficiency by 74.29% on average relative to the four prior frameworks. Organizations generated automatically by language models improved these measures by 43.63% and 52.53%, respectively. These advantages persisted across missions and underlying language models. Notably, collective performance was not monotonically determined by model scale. Analysis of long-horizon missions showed that hierarchical organization enabled teams to preserve concurrent activity within specialized groups while coordinating ordered transitions between mission phases.
items.title: ORCH: Organizational Principles Enable Collective Intelligence in Embodied AI

items.summary: This dataset accompanies “Population-scale burden analysis of rare damaging coding variants identifies novel risk genes for Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias and Parkinson’s disease and related disorders” by Le Guen, Peña-Tauber and colleagues. The release contains 16 gzip-compressed, tab-delimited gene-based burden summary-statistic files covering Alzheimer’s disease (AD), Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias (ADRD), Parkinson’s disease (PD), and Parkinson’s disease and related disorders (PDRD); combined-proxy and direct-diagnosis ascertainment; and all-ancestry (ALL) and European-ancestry (EUR) analyses. The files share 61 columns and contain 1,000,189 retained gene/mask analysis rows in total, including nonsignificant results. The four nested masks comprise high-confidence loss-of-function variants alone or together with qualifying missense variants at REVEL thresholds of 0.75, 0.50 or 0.25. The associated manuscript specifies GRCh38 coordinates. The primary discovery analyses are AD combined-proxy ALL and PD combined-proxy ALL. EUR analyses are secondary ancestry analyses; AD-direct and PD-direct are secondary, nested phenotype-sensitivity analyses. All ADRD/PDRD analyses are diagnostic-sensitivity comparisons. Combined-proxy includes direct cases and family-history-only proxy cases, not proxy cases alone. Phenotype definitions and ancestry strata overlap and are not independent replication datasets. The release explicitly separates effect estimation from association evidence. REGENIE-only effect estimates combine compatible binary-outcome burden models from UK Biobank, All of Us and ADSP for AD/ADRD, or UK Biobank, All of Us and AMP-PD for PD/PDRD. Combined-proxy cohort effects use the revised exact common-control mixture-model inversion under kappa=0.5. ADES stage-1 estimates from Holstege et al. (2022) are reported separately because their ordinal summed-dosage model differs from the REGENIE binary-outcome maximum-allele burden model. Eligible ADES and REGENIE results are integrated through effective-sample-size-weighted signed-Z evidence; no ADES-inclusive pooled odds ratio is calculated. Use P_OVERALL or LOG10P_OVERALL for final association evidence, and the BETA_REGENIE, SE_REGENIE and REGENIE odds-ratio/confidence-interval columns for the pooled REGENIE effect estimate. AD/ADRD overall evidence falls back to REGENIE when eligible ADES evidence is unavailable. ADES does not contribute to PD/PDRD. The same ADES source is reused across AD-family comparisons and ancestry strata. The README and column dictionary define all fields, missing-value conventions, numerical precision and interpretation. A public manifest and checksums document all 16 files. The dataset contains aggregate gene-level results, not individual-level genotypes or single-variant summary statistics. items.summary: As large language models (LLMs) become widely deployed, their outputs can be copied, transformed, and redistributed at scale without reliable evidence of origin, creating risks for trust, accountability, intellectual property (IP) protection, and high-stakes decision-making. LLM watermarking addresses this problem by embedding detectable signals into text during or after generation. However, existing methods vary in design assumptions, threat models, and evaluation criteria, while deployment choices such as watermark placement, detection authority, and key management affect reliability, security, and scalability. This paper systematizes LLM watermarking as provenance infrastructure for large-scale data ecosystems. We organize existing approaches along four deployment dimensions: insertion point, verification authority, operational state, and transformation threat model, and relate them to the big data requirements of Volume, Velocity, Variety, Veracity, and Value. We further introduce a Big Data Watermarking Readiness framework centered on four deployment workloads: online generation, streaming detection, transformation pipelines, and ecosystem governance. The framework connects these workloads to system-level requirements including throughput, false-positive control, robustness, cross-domain reliability, governance, and downstream utility. Our analysis highlights a gap between benchmark performance and deployment readiness: false positives accumulate at scale, repeated transformations weaken watermark signals, computational overhead can limit online deployment, and centralized verification can create governance bottlenecks. We conclude with an evaluation blueprint and research directions for scalable, trustworthy provenance in big data ecosystems.
items.title: LLM Watermarking as Big Data Provenance: A Deployment-Oriented Systematization

items.summary: This repository contains two LC–MS/MS raw data files (and .mgf versions if needed), associated search parameters, and curated FASTA databases generated from purified fibrinogen clots crosslinked by endogenous FXIIIa or recombinant transglutaminase 2 (TG2). These samples represent a controlled benchmark system for evaluating crosslink-mass spectrometry (XL-MS) software performance on non-cleavable enzymatic Q–K isopeptide bonds. Unlike conventional chemical crosslinkers, these transglutaminase-mediated crosslinks are zero-length modifications formed by ammonia (NH₃) loss, creating unique challenges for false discovery control and site assignment. The datasets are provided to enable transparent, community-driven comparison of XL search engines and to advance methodological development in enzymatic crosslink identification.

S-AI-WorldModel addresses this question through an explicit canonical representation, regulated update dynamics, computable commitment conditions, and a source-only symbolic reconstruction pipeline. The implemented source-only action-model pipeline combines ActionParamAgent, PreconditionAgent, EffectAgent, guarded semantic dynamics, structural commit, parse recovery, result-state completion, and precondition anchoring. items.summary: Modern large language model research agents, commonly marketed under the label deep research, are highly capable at locating sources, verifying claims, and synthesizing existing literature into structured reports. This capability has not translated into a comparable capacity for scientific discovery. We argue that this gap has a specific, testable cause, which we call literature attracti on: the more strongly a generation process is grounded in retrieved literature, the more its outputs converge toward concepts already dominant in that literature, at the expense of novelty. We separate four quantities that are routinely conflated in evaluations of AI research systems: research depth, research novelty, research validity, and research value. We review the current frontier of deep research systems and automated science pipelines, describe the attention-level mechanisms that plausibly cause literature attraction in retrieval-augmented generation, and propose a controlled experimental protocol to measure the novelty-grounding tradeoff dir ectly, using embedding-based and graph-based novelty metrics, a temporal hold-out benchmark, and human expert validation. We then outline an architectural response: a two-stage exploit-then-explore pipeline in which a quality-diversity search process is used to deliberately push hypothesis generation into regions of the concept space that are underrepresented in the retrieved literature, while an adversarial falsification agent constrains the resulting hypotheses to remain scientificall y testable. We close with a proposed output format, the research novelty report, that reports where a generated hypothesis sits relative to existing knowledge rather than asserting that it is novel. This paper is a research proposal and experimental design; it does not claim to have already demonstrated the phenomenon it sets out to measure.
items.title: Escaping the Literature: Exploring New Scientific Ideas with Large Language Models

items.summary: Electric vehicles (EVs) experience significant  driving  range degradation in low ambient temperature conditions, primarily due to the elevated energy demand of heating system.  T his paper proposes  an optimal  control strategy for a  positive temperature coefficient ( PTC )  heater-based electric minibus  heating system ,  which is  aimed to  exploit actuators’ redundancy for  energy consumption  minimization  and driving range extension . The strategy  optimally  allocates  control inputs  of multiple actuators  to  provide  heating power demand ed  by a superimposed proportional-integral (PI)  feedback  controller of the  passenger  cabin air temperatur e .  The  optimal  allocation maps prescri be  coolant pump flow, blower air   flow, and inlet air temperature references , and they  are obtained by comprehensive simulations of a high-fidelity multi-physics heating system model over a wide range of quasi-stationary operating conditions .   A low-level PI controller is further designed for the full ,  allocation-related range of operating points to track the  allocated  inlet air temperature reference, while commanding the PTC heater power.   The overall control strategy is validated through co-simulation with a high-fidelity vehicle model  in comparison with an industry baseline strategy , demonstrating a considerable energy consumption reduction in both quasi-stationary and transient (heat up) conditions, as well as improved control performance in terms of shorter heat up intervals.
items.title: Optimal Control Allocation Strategy for an Energy-efficient PTC Heater-based Electric Vehicle Passenger Cabin Heating System

items.summary: A 0.1° monthly and daily terrestrial water storage anomaly (TWSA) product for the Ganga (Ganges) River Basin, 2000–2025 , together with the source code, the inputs, and the full evaluation record that produced it. GRACE and GRACE-FO JPL RL06 mascons are spatially downscaled by fitting a predictor–TWSA relation across mascons; every mascon's area-weighted aggregate is then forced back onto the observed value. The monthly field is disaggregated to daily under an exact monthly constraint, its within-month shape supplied by the ERA5-Land water balance with nothing fitted at the daily scale. Per-pixel uncertainty is reported as four separate terms rather than one number, because only some of them are measurable against an observation. What changed in v1.0.1, and what did not. The data are unchanged. The three product netCDFs, the monthly and daily COGs, the trend field and every input and intermediate archive are the same files already in this record — if you have them, there is nothing to download again, and any analysis built on v1.0.0 stands. Four files change, all of them code or documentation: grace-grb-1.0.1.zip , the source at the new tag, which adds main/trend_regions.py and the scripts behind three manuscript figures; evaluation_tables.zip , which gains trend_by_region.csv ; figures.zip , which gains those three plates; and DATA_README.md . The version exists for reproducibility rather than revision: the regional trend figures quoted in the paper were computed from a region definition that had never been committed, so a reader holding the archived trend field could not reproduce them. That definition is now in the archive, it is checked to partition the basin, and the paper cites this version. What is imposed and what is learned. Each mascon's level and linear trend are taken from GRACE rather than learned from the predictors — the secular signal here is groundwater abstraction, and no reanalysis simulates pumping. Only the sub-mascon anomaly is modelled, from 78 predictor features built on ERA5-Land and nine covariates, seven of them static and two annual cropland fractions held constant after 2022. Mass conservation then forces every mascon mean back onto the observation by a minimum-norm correction. Agreement with GRACE at mascon scale is therefore arithmetic, not evidence of skill : the basin mean of this product reproduces the GRACE basin mean at r = 1.00000, RMSE 0.27 mm. We state that plainly so it is not mistaken for validation. Held-out performance. Skill is reported only where it can be measured — at spatial units the model never saw, at times it never saw, and against an independent observation. Spatial (leave-one-mascon-out, 19 folds with a neighbour buffer): RMSE 88.2 mm, R² 0.638, NSE 0.635 over 83,309 held-out cell-months. Cluster bootstrap over mascons (2,000 resamples): RMSE 82.1–95.1 mm, R² 0.580–0.694. Temporal (whole months held out): interior gap-filling RMSE 71.7 mm (R² 0.775); scattered months 74.5 mm (0.713), a random split and so optimistic — each withheld month keeps its neighbours in training; out-of-record extrapolation 91.1 mm (0.730) . The last is the regime the post-2024 months live in. Independent (656 quality-controlled CGWB dug wells): at basin scale the downscaled field reaches r = 0.814, RMSE 57.0 mm against a bilinear-interpolation baseline at r = 0.742, RMSE 73.1 mm. Skill is strongly scale-dependent: median R² is 0.48 per mascon but 0.19 per well, and NSE exceeds zero at only 168 of 656 wells. Neither side is ground truth — a well is a point head times an estimated specific yield, the product a 0.1° cell from a 3° mascon — so the scale dependence is reported as the result rather than a single pooled number. items.summary: Background: Surface roughness is an important characteristic of resin composite restorations and may be influenced by material composition and finishing and polishing procedures. Objective: To evaluate changes in surface roughness (Ra) of nanofilled, nanohybrid, and microhybrid resin composites after sequential finishing and polishing and to compare their final surface roughness. Materials and Methods: S ixty disc-shaped specimens (8 mm × 2 mm; shade A2) were fabricated using Filtek Z350 XT, IPS Empress Direct, and Filtek Z250 (n = 20 per material). Fifteen specimens per material underwent a standardized finishing and polishing protocol using fine- and extra-fine-grit diamond burs followed by sequential Sof-Lex discs, while five specimens per material remained untreated as controls. Surface roughness was measured using a Mitutoyo SJ-210 contact profilometer at baseline   and after the intervention. Because specimen-level identification was not preserved between measurement sessions, baseline and final measurements were analyzed as independent observations using independent-samples t-tests, with Welch’s correction when required. Final Ra values among materials were compared using one-way ANOVA followed by Tukey HSD tests (α = 0.05). Results: All three experimental composites showed statistically significant increases in Ra after finishing and polishing (all p < 0.001), whereas no statistically significant changes were observed in the untreated controls (all p > 0.05). Mean Ra increased from 0.085 to 0.181 μm for IPS Empress Direct, from 0.111 to 0.186 μm for Filtek Z350 XT, and from 0.122 to 0.195 μm for Filtek Z250. Final Ra values did not differ significantly among the three materials (F(2,42) = 0.559, p = 0.576). Conclusions: Sequential finishing and polishing significantly increased surface roughness relative to the strip-polymerized baseline surfaces of all three resin composites, without statistically significant differences in final Ra among the materials. The final mean Ra values remained below the predefined 0.2 μm surface-roughness threshold. Under the experimental conditions evaluated, post-polishing surface roughness could not be predicted solely on the basis of nanofilled, nanohybrid, or microhybrid filler classification.
items.title: Surface Roughness of Nanofilled, Nanohybrid, and Microhy-brid Resin Composites After Sequential Finishing and Polish-ing: An In Vitro Comparative Study

items.summary: Abstract Background  Thyroid dysfunction is one of the most common endocrine disorders affecting metabolic activity, psychological well-being, and gastrointestinal function.(1,2) Patients frequently experience elevated thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) levels, stress, bloating, impaired digestion, reduced metabolic efficiency, and decreased quality of life. Although conventional treatment effectively restores thyroid hormone balance in many patients, complementary therapeutic interventions are increasingly being explored to improve overall clinical outcomes and patient-reported health status.  Aim  To evaluate the effect of a Teacurry Thyro Herb Tea for Thyroid on thyroid function, perceived stress, gastrointestinal symptoms, and participant-reported global improvement among adults with thyroid dysfunction.  Materials and Methods:  A prospective, single-arm interventional clinical study was conducted involving  22 adult participants  diagnosed with thyroid dysfunction. Baseline demographic characteristics including age, body weight, height, and body mass index (BMI) were recorded. Clinical assessments included serum thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH), perceived stress score (0–40 scale), gastrointestinal symptoms related to bloating, digestion, and metabolism, and Participant Global Impression of Change (PGIC). All parameters were assessed before and after the intervention. The composition of the study formulation will be described separately. Statistical analysis was performed using appropriate descriptive and inferential statistical methods, and statistical significance was considered at  p  < 0.05.  Results:  The intervention demonstrated an overall improvement in multiple clinical outcomes. Mean serum TSH decreased from  10.27 to 3.77 mIU/L , while mean perceived stress scores decreased from  20.45 to 13.18 . Improvement in gastrointestinal symptoms and PGIC scores was observed in the majority of participants. Perceived stress scores decreased in a substantial proportion of participants, indicating improvement in psychological well-being. Gastrointestinal symptoms such as bloating and impaired digestion improved from mild or moderate severity to normal or minimal symptoms in the majority of cases. Participant-reported outcomes also demonstrated favorable changes, with PGIC scores increasing in most participants, suggesting meaningful overall clinical improvement. The intervention was generally well tolerated, and no serious adverse events were documented during the study period.  Conclusion:  The findings of this prospective clinical study suggest that the investigated Teacurry Thyro Herb Tea for Thyroid may contribute to improved thyroid function, reduction in perceived stress, better gastrointestinal health, and enhanced patient-reported quality of life in adults with thyroid dysfunction. These preliminary findings support the potential role of the formulation as a complementary therapeutic option. Larger randomized controlled clinical trials with extended follow-up are warranted to confirm these observations and establish long-term efficacy and safety.   Keywords: Thyroid Dysfunction; Thyroid Stimulating Hormone; TSH; Teacurry Thyro Herb Tea for Thyroid; Teacurry Thyroid Tea; Teacurry; Thyroid Tea; Herbal Tea for Thyroid; Complementary ##plugin
items.title: Effect of a Plant-Based Herbal Tea Formulation "Teacurry Thyro Herb Tea for Thyroid" on Thyroid Function, TSH Levels, Gastrointestinal Symptoms and Participant-Reported Global Improvement in Adults with Thyroid Dysfunction: Real-World Evidence Clinical Study

items.summary: Reliability Beyond Accuracy in Crop Classification Benchmarks (Supplementary Materials) Introduction: Near-perfect crop-label accuracy can conceal uncertainty, perturbation sensitivity, and weak explanations. This study evaluates these reliability dimensions without treating benchmark classification as agronomic recommendation. Materials and Methods: Ten classifiers were evaluated using five matched stratified fitting, validation, and test partitions on a 2,200-record crop-label benchmark and an independent 3,810-record rice-grain benchmark. A Calibrated Selective Forest combined Random Forest, validation-fitted temperature scaling, and confidence-based abstention. Analyses included feature and component ablations, probability calibration, Gaussian input perturbations, computational cost, and explanation fidelity. Results: Mean crop-label accuracy was 99.59% for Random Forest, 99.23% for XGBoost, and 98.32% for FT-Transformer. Random Forest calibration reduced mean expected calibration error from 0.0449 to 0.0038. At a 0.95 threshold, calibrated selection retained 98.59% of predictions with 0.091% mean selective error. Under perturbations of 0.20 training standard deviations, its accuracy fell to 86.96% and selective error rose to 4.29%. On rice grains, Random Forest accuracy was 91.71%, and calibration did not improve every probability metric. Local explanation rankings were often stable despite a median neighborhood weighted R² of 0.293 under the specified local interpretable model-agnostic explanations (LIME) configuration. Conclusions: Accuracy, calibration, selective reliability, and explanation fidelity are distinct properties. The composite pipeline provides an auditable benchmark procedure, not a new learning algorithm or a validated farm recommendation system. Geographic and temporal agronomic validation remain necessary.
items.title: Reliability Beyond Accuracy in Crop Classification Benchmarks (Supplementary Materials)

items.summary: AUST_2026_BAT is a global bathymetric model developed using multi-scale marine gravity anomaly features, fully connected deep neural networks (FCDNNs), and an adaptive multi-factor spatial partitioning (AMFSP) framework. The dataset covers 180°W–180°E and 75°S–75°N at a spatial resolution of 1′ × 1′. The oceanic portion represents the modeled bathymetry, while land elevations are filled using the land component of GEBCO_2025, forming a spatially continuous topographic–bathymetric grid over the entire model domain. AUST_2026_BAT was generated using SIO V33.1 marine gravity anomalies and quality-controlled shipborne bathymetric observations from the National Centers for Environmental Information (NCEI). The marine gravity field was decomposed into multi-scale features, including long-wavelength gravity anomalies (LG), short-wavelength gravity anomalies (SG), and their corresponding residual components (RLG and RSG), to represent gravity–bathymetry relationships at different spatial scales and retain complementary residual information for bathymetric prediction. To account for regional variations in seafloor morphology, gravity–bathymetry relationships, observational coverage, and coastal conditions, the global domain was divided into 60 primary 30° × 30° regions and further partitioned using the AMFSP framework based on water depth, seafloor slope, gravity anomaly, shipborne sounding density, and distance from the coastline. FCDNN models were then trained for individual subregions, and predictions in overlapping areas were merged using a standard-deviation-weighted blending strategy to generate the final continuous global bathymetric surface. Independent validation using shipborne bathymetric observations shows good overall agreement between AUST_2026_BAT and measured seafloor depths. Comparisons with existing global bathymetric models, including GEBCO_2025, SIO topo_27.1, and SRTM15+ V2.7, indicate lower overall prediction errors for AUST_2026_BAT, with the improvements being more pronounced in deep-water regions and generally consistent performance across the major ocean basins.
items.title: AUST_2026_BAT: A Global Bathymetry Model Derived from Multi-Scale Marine Gravity Anomalies Using Fully Connected Deep Neural Networks and Adaptive Multi-Factor Spatial Partitioning

items.summary: Python package and command-line tool that estimates the share of variance in an antimicrobial resistance phenotype carried by the lineages of a bacterial collection, from a lineage label and a susceptibility call or a recorded dilution, and refuses the estimate where the collection cannot support one. One collection admits three quantities and the package reports them apart: the lineage-membership share, what a rule scored out of sample reaches, with a lineage bootstrap; the design-corrected component ratio of the same collection, with an interval exact under the Gaussian one-way model by inversion of a noncentral F; and the superpopulation share for the species, with a chi-square layer on the number of lineages. Each is scored against its own truth on 135 simulated cells from five lineages to a thousand, and each sits behind a gate that refuses where the collection cannot identify the quantity or the residuals contradict the law the interval assumes, the coverage of each having been measured. A binary share is restated on the latent scale of the threshold model beside the observed scale. The lineage label may be a sequence type, a core-genome or SNP cluster, or a serovar, so the same estimate can be read at two typing resolutions. For a difference in non-wild-type prevalence between two collections it applies the Kitagawa decomposition to split the difference into a lineage-composition component and a within-lineage rate component, with a shared-support gate calibrated against measured interval coverage, a test for lineage labels that are differentially and informatively missing, and Benjamini-Yekutieli control within each component family of the antimicrobial panel, valid whatever the dependence between agents. Ships a Streptococcus suis case study (677 isolates, 650 porcine and 27 human, with full data provenance) read at population-cluster and at sequence-type resolution, together with a 720,000-decomposition calibration study and a head-to-head comparison against lineage-adjusted logistic regression. The package reads two tables and never a genome. A susceptibility panel is read at its recorded resolution: a dichotomised call and a recorded dilution are both intervals on the log2 concentration scale and enter one interval likelihood, so the input mode changes how much an observation carries rather than what is estimated. The interval is exact where every reading is a point and calibrated by simulation where a reading is an interval, and the tested wells are taken from the recorded values unless the panel is supplied. Each share carries an e-value; a run that declares the intake each isolate arrived in also carries the running product over intakes, a test supermartingale that may be read after any intake, with the panel decision taken on the log scale so that evidence too strong for a float is still evidence. False-discovery control across the panel holds under arbitrary dependence. The attribution is exercised outside the shipped cohorts on fifty organisms of one NCBI Pathogen Detection release, each taken at the release accession the retrieval recorded: every agent of every cohort that reaches the estimator leaves one record, estimated or refused with the condition that failed, 192 cells are estimated in twelve species and 44 admitted by the support gate in six, and every cell carries a permuted-label control. items.summary: Calibration release: the package's no-shipped-coefficients policy finally comes with the tool that closes the loop. Every shipped set carries the caveat that lever arms depend on material, mode pair, excitation and substrate; calibrate_lever_arms turns reference measurements you control -- a strain-stage sweep, a gated sweep, any points with known (strain, density) -- into your own fitted coefficient matrix, with uncertainties and provenance. New in ramansep.calibration calibrate_lever_arms : weighted least-squares fit of the (m, 2) lever-arm matrix, one linear problem per mode on the shared reference design. With shift sigmas the parameter covariance is the exact known-noise Gauss-Markov result and a per-mode chi-square consistency check comes back with it; without sigmas the covariance uses the residual variance, which is why that path refuses fewer than three reference points instead of inventing an error bar. Identifiability refused, not fudged : reference states collinear in the (strain, density) plane (a strain-only sweep, or gating that strains proportionally) cannot separately determine the two arms of any mode -- the fit raises with an explanation instead of returning one of infinitely many minimizers. CalibrationResult.coefficients() packages a two-mode calibration as a ModeCoefficients with a MANDATORY provenance string; result.K feeds MultiModeModel directly for m > 2. Anchors (asserted in the tests, not stated) Noise-free shifts from a known matrix are recovered to machine precision, with zero estimated uncertainty. The hand-built normal-equation solution agrees with an independent QR solve ( numpy.linalg.lstsq on the whitened system) to 1e-10. The orthogonal unit design {(1,0), (0,1)} with unit sigmas has EXACTLY the identity parameter covariance -- the closed form, not an approximation. Seeded Monte-Carlo scatter of the fitted arms matches the reported sigmas. Degenerate and malformed reference sets raise (collinear designs, n = 1, n = 2 without sigmas, non-positive sigmas, non-finite shifts). The full round trip -- calibrate on synthetic references, package the coefficients, invert forward-generated maps through SeparationModel -- returns the input strain and density maps to 1e-10. 50 tests across Python 3.9-3.13. Install: pip install -U ramansep .
items.title: ramansep: two-mode separation of strain and carrier density in 2D-material Raman maps

items.summary: This repository provides the supplementary materials and reproducibility package for the manuscript “Spatial–Temporal Hedging in Cross-Border Logistics under Heterogeneous Evidence Quality: A Wasserstein DRO Approach.” The repository contains the computational inputs, scenario data, experimental results, source code, and supplementary numerical outputs used in the study. items.summary: Per-pixel  active-flame  image–mask chips from  Sentinel-2  covering  25 large California wildfires  (acquisitions spanning 2020–2026). The deposit contains  2,148  co-registered pairs of false-colour composites and segmentation masks. Each chip is  512 × 512 pixels at 20 m  (~10.24 km across), rendered as a fixed-stretch RGB composite ( R = B12 / SWIR2 ,  G = B11 / SWIR1 ,  B = B8A / NIR ) so flaming combustion is separable from cloud, smoke, fresh char, and bright reflective surfaces. Masks were generated automatically with a  modified HOTMAP SWIR hotspot rule  (confirmed flame where B12 and B12/B8A exceed conservative thresholds, plus a connected growth tier for cooler front margins). Pixel values are  0 = background ,  1 = active fire , and  255 = no-data  (outside the acquisition footprint). The corpus uses a  leak-free fire holdout : whole incidents are assigned to partitions ( 18 train / 3 validation / 4 test ), so evaluation measures transfer to unseen fires rather than random chips from the same landscape. This archive includes: images/  and  masks/  (2,148 PNG files each) summary.csv  (chip-level metadata) partitions.csv  (fire → split assignment) analyst_review/hand_masks/  ( 233  independently reviewed test chips;  54%  of the test split), for quantifying weak-label agreement at chip/cluster level Companion  code , labelling protocol, baseline training scripts, and manuscript figures are available at:   https://github.com/MohammadrezaNarimaniUCDavis/California_Sentinel2_Active_Fire_Dataset This dataset supports a data article prepared for submission to  Data in Brief (Elsevier).
items.title: California Sentinel-2 Active-Fire Segmentation Dataset

items.summary: The Earth That Heard is not presented as a literary reconstruction built around biblical verses. It records a textual architecture that the author argues is already present in the Torah itself — a structure that emerged through fifteen years of research into Biblical Hebrew morphology, roots, recurring letter patterns, and the internal organization of the text. The essay traces a continuous thread from the murder of Abel in Genesis to Joshua’s altar on Mount Ebal. Motifs that initially appear independent — earth and blood, firstfruit and firstborn, field and El Shaddai, rising and place, sacrifice, Shechem, the opening of the earth, and the return of the firstfruits — progressively converge into a single narrative structure. The central proposal is that Abel’s unfinished offering, Cain’s failure, and the wounded earth are not abandoned episodes: their resolution unfolds across the Torah and reaches completion in Joshua. The work explicitly separates three epistemic levels: Text — what the biblical text states; Reading — what emerges when distant passages are compared; and Implication — the larger interpretation suggested by the resulting structure. The pattern is also tested quantitatively. The present essay contains 136 key verses; the original connection-density test was performed on a pre-set group of 124 verses selected by the narrative. Using the Control Alphabet / Mandatory Root morphology developed in The Road and the Place , the observed network produced Z = 19.37 (p < 0.0002) against 5,000 random permutations. A second, deliberately simpler test removes the seven control letters א, מ, ת, נ, י, ה, ו from every word and performs direct string matching with no root database; it still yields Z = 10.29 (p < 0.0002) , with the same major long-range connections rising to the top. A raw-word test remains significant at Z = 5.17 (p = 0.0013) . A separate anthology comparison tests whether similarly chosen biblical themes automatically generate the same effect. The Ebal/Shechem axis reaches Z = 17.35 , compared with Covenant Z = 10.07 , Jerusalem/Temple Z = 1.60 , Joseph Z = −8.13 , and Tabernacle Z = −7.16 . The result does not statistically prove the theological interpretation; it shows that the textual concentration being interpreted is itself measurable and unusual. A scientific appendix further examines comparative anatomical and genomic parallels associated with one of the essay’s most unexpected motifs, while explicitly distinguishing scientific observation from midrashic interpretation. After fifteen years of work, the author does not regard this as a story invented to fit the text, but as part of a larger architecture that the text itself gradually disclosed — a structure he considers himself fortunate to have uncovered, even if only in part, and to place on record now. Bilingual publication: Hebrew original and English edition.
items.title: The Earth That Listened — The Hidden Timeline from Genesis to Joshua

items.summary: Replication data and code for an analysis of how allocation procedures shape which Italian municipalities obtain Recovery and Resilience Facility resources, and whether they convert them into completed works. The package covers 68,990 projects implemented by municipal governments across 36 plan measures, extracted from the OpenPNRR REST API at the ReGiS extraction date of 13 June 2026. Each project carries a coded allocation regime — open window, competitive, administrative assignment, or decentralised regional selection — reconstructed from the administrative activation procedure and, where that field is blank, from the founding decrees of the measures concerned. Contents: the analytical dataset (31 variables); a codebook; a procedure coding table with the normative source of every coding decision; a crosswalk matching 39 measures to the official monitoring of the statutory 40 per cent Southern allocation obligation; municipality-level residuals from the implementation models; global Moran's I under three alternative spatial weight matrices; local Moran statistics on the downstream residual; the reported model results; the extraction script; and a replication script that reproduces the dataset and every estimate from the raw inputs. WHY THIS PACKAGE IS NECESSARY. The primary source is neither versioned nor stable. While this dataset was being constructed, the same endpoint returned 280,767 records dated 26 February 2026 and, hours later, 291,387 records dated 13 June 2026, while the published CSV files carried 298,338 records; between those two responses the numeric identifiers of both projects and implementing organisations were reassigned. A replication attempt that re-downloaded from source would not reproduce these figures, and no version parameter is available to request a specific extraction. The archived snapshot in this package is the only reproducible reference. TWO TRAPS THAT FAIL SILENTLY. ISTAT codes and fiscal codes lose leading zeros if read as numeric, producing empty joins with no error; in the source organisation register, fiscal codes are stored inconsistently with and without leading zeros, and normalising to eleven digits reduces 13,126 records labelled as municipalities to 7,902 distinct entities. Numeric project identifiers are not stable join keys, coinciding across extractions in only 52.9 per cent of cases; the CUP is not unique. Use the local project code. SPATIAL ANALYSIS. Municipal geometries are the official Istat boundaries at 1 January 2021, joined on the six-digit code. The boundary file is not redistributed here and should be obtained from Istat. Three weight matrices are reported — queen contiguity, eight nearest neighbours and a fifty-kilometre distance band — because they are not interchangeable on subsamples: queen contiguity strands as isolates not only islands but mainland municipalities whose neighbours do not belong to the subsample, and those units are dropped silently from the statistic. Isolate counts are reported for every specification. The duration residual was the pre-specified primary diagnostic and the downstream residual was examined subsequently; both are reported in that order. The package contains no personal data: all implementing bodies are public administrations.
items.title: Allocation regimes and the territorial conversion of recovery funds: replication package for 71,548 municipal projects under Italy's National Recovery and Resilience Plan

items.summary: Collective intelligence depends not only on the capabilities of individual members, but also on how those members are organized. Yet artificial multi-agent systems are typically assembled using fixed organizational structures, even when the physical tasks they perform impose fundamentally different coordination requirements. Here we show that principles from human organization theory can be operationalized to organize large, heterogeneous collectives of embodied artificial agents. We introduce ORCH (Organizing Roles and Coordination Hierarchies), which constructs task-specific hierarchical organizations by combining pooled interdependence for work that can proceed concurrently with sequential interdependence for work governed by prerequisite relationships. Across 25 wildfire-response missions spanning reconnaissance, rescue, transportation, resource management, containment and suppression, we evaluated teams of up to 50 heterogeneous agents using eight large language models. Organizations constructed using these principles consistently outperformed four representative embodied multi-agent approaches across mission outcome, execution efficiency, exploration and computational resource use. Human-designed ORCH organizations improved final score by 63.97% and execution efficiency by 74.29% on average relative to the four prior frameworks. Organizations generated automatically by language models improved these measures by 43.63% and 52.53%, respectively. These advantages persisted across missions and underlying language models. Notably, collective performance was not monotonically determined by model scale. Analysis of long-horizon missions showed that hierarchical organization enabled teams to preserve concurrent activity within specialized groups while coordinating ordered transitions between mission phases.
items.title: ORCH: Organizational Principles Enable Collective Intelligence in Embodied AI
